overview.text: Josh Hawley is a Republican lawyer and U.S. senator representing Missouri. Raised in Lexington, Missouri, he studied at Stanford University and Yale Law School, then worked as a constitutional lawyer, including in cases before the U.S. Supreme Court. Before entering the Senate, he served as Missouri’s attorney general from 2017 to 2019. He began his Senate service on January 3, 2019, and is listed by the Senate as a current Missouri senator. His public profile is also associated with January 6, 2021: a House committee hearing described him raising a fist toward protesters outside the Capitol before they breached the building, characterizing the gesture as solidarity with them.

key_facts.text: Hawley studied at Stanford University, graduating in 2002, and earned his law degree from Yale Law School in 2006.
He served as Missouri’s attorney general from 2017 to 2019 before taking his Senate seat.
The Senate lists Hawley as a Republican senator for Missouri, with service beginning January 3, 2019.
Missouri’s official 2025–2026 manual says Hawley argued cases before the U.S. Supreme Court and was a lead attorney in Hobby Lobby and Hosanna-Tabor.

At a July 21, 2022, House committee hearing, Representative Elaine Luria described Hawley raising his fist toward protesters at the Capitol on January 6, 2021; this is the committee’s characterization of the gesture.
